newsitem.title: USA: Excel's Ottumwa, Iowa pork plant slowly reopens.
newsitem.headline: Excel's Ottumwa, Iowa pork plant slowly reopens.

text.p: Operations at Excel Corp's fire-damaged Ottumwa, Iowa hog slaughter and pork processing plant were slowly coming back on line after reopening Monday, a company spokesman said.
"We had everybody come back on Monday and we're going real slow to get everyone re-acclimated safely," said Mark Klein, Excel spokesman.
A fire and explosion closed the plant on January 26.
Excel Corp is a subsidiary of Cargill Inc.
The plant's 1,300 employees returned to work on Monday, but it will take several weeks to gradually get back to the daily slaughter capacity of 9,600 head, Klein said.
While the Ottumwa plant was being repaired, the slack in operations were taken up at Excel's hog facilities in Beardstown, Ill. and Marshall, Mo.
As the Ottumwa plant output gradually gets up to speed, operations at the other two plants will wind down to pre-fire levels, Klein said.
